exposure: Prolonged dystocic labor (PDL) with Labor Neuraxial Analgesia (LNA)
Fetal head malpositions (Occiput Posterior Position, Persistent Occiput Posterior Position, transverse position, asynclitism)
outcome: Enkephalinergic neuro fibers (En) content and morphology in the Lower Uterine Segment (LUS)
cohort: The study included 38 patients undergoing urgent cesarean section due to prolonged dystocic labor and 37 patients submitted to elective cesarean section.
finding: The analysis of Lower Uterine Segment (LUS) samples showed a significant reduction in enkephalinergic neuro fibers (En) in patients with prolonged dystocic labor compared to those undergoing elective cesarean section, suggesting that drugs used in labor neuraxial analgesia may be ineffective for 'dystocic pain' caused by LUS overdistension and fetal malpositions.
mod_finding: The study suggests that when dystocia is diagnosed by intrapartum ultrasonography, repeated ineffective top-up drug administrations during labor neuraxial analgesia should cease, and labor should transition to operative vaginal delivery or cesarean section.
